precepts.text: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates? That examine yourselves is the same thing Jeremiah said. Let us search and try our ways.
precepts.point: Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people. Looked up in class: offscouring is a rare noun that means physical dirt or refuse cleaned off an object, or a person rejected by society as an outcast. Literal waste, dirt, grime or scum scrubbed off a dirty surface. Social outcast, a person treated as scum, trash, or a pariah by society. Biblical use found in older translations like the King James Bible, such as 1 Corinthians 4:13 and Lamentations 3:45, to describe how lowly or despised the apostles and the people of Jerusalem felt.
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says, “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” Paul is talking about the same thing: “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” That examine yourselves is the same thing Jeremiah said: let us search and try our ways.

This is a lot of times what we as a people do not want to do: examine ourselves. What is wrong with me? What is wrong with you? Who raised you? Why do you act that way? Why do you do the things that you do?

“Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?” You have to prove your own self, whether Christ is in you or not. And that is where turning again to the Lord starts. Jeremiah goes on, “We have transgressed and have rebelled: thou hast not pardoned”, and that is why we are in this state, the condition we are in now. A people who will not examine themselves will never see why the Lord has covered himself with a cloud, and will never turn again to him.

precepts.text: And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed. Salvation is near. It is high time that we wake up from our sleep. In order to wake up, we must start by examining ourselves.
precepts.point: Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people. Looked up in class: offscouring is a rare noun that means physical dirt or refuse cleaned off an object, or a person rejected by society as an outcast. Literal waste, dirt, grime or scum scrubbed off a dirty surface. Social outcast, a person treated as scum, trash, or a pariah by society. Biblical use found in older translations like the King James Bible, such as 1 Corinthians 4:13 and Lamentations 3:45, to describe how lowly or despised the apostles and the people of Jerusalem felt.
precepts.why:
Paul says: “And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.” Salvation is near. It is high time that we wake up from our sleep.

In order to wake up, we must start by examining ourselves, which is what Jeremiah calls for: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” What is wrong with me? What is wrong with you? Who raised you? Why do you act that way? Why do you do the things that you do?

Waking up is not only knowing who we are. It is searching our own ways, seeing that “We have transgressed and have rebelled”, and turning again to the Lord, lifting up our heart with our hands unto God in the heavens. The time is short and salvation is nearer than when we first believed, so there is no time left to stay asleep in the condition we are in.

precepts.text: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet. I would not know what sin is but by the law. I would not know what lust is. By studying the word of God you are able to self-examine. You are able to search and try your ways.

Literal waste, dirt, grime or scum scrubbed off a dirty surface. Social outcast, a person treated as scum, trash, or a pariah by society. Biblical use found in older translations like the King James Bible, such as 1 Corinthians 4:13 and Lamentations 3:45, to describe how lowly or despised the apostles and the people of Jerusalem felt.
precepts.why:
How do we search and try our ways? Paul shows it: “What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.” I would not know what sin is, but by the law. I would not know what lust is, except the law told me.

So by studying the word of God, you are able to self-examine. You are able to search and try your ways, by studying and reading the word of God. That is what Paul said, and it is what Jeremiah said: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.”

Without the law a man has no measure to try himself by; he thinks what he is doing is fine. With the law in front of him, he can see where “We have transgressed and have rebelled”, and why the Lord has not pardoned. The law is the mirror, and the one who reads it is the one who can turn again.

precepts.text: They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me: meaning he would never get out. It's talking about Israel in captivity, which goes with political prisoners who have been in there a long time.
precepts.point: Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.
precepts.why:
After interpreting the butler's dream, Joseph asked him, “think on me when it shall be well with thee,” and “make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:” “For indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.” He wanted out of that dungeon.

Notice the prison is called a dungeon. Lamentations uses the same word: “They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.” To cast a stone upon him means he would never get out. It is speaking of Israel in captivity.

That goes with our political prisoners, who have been in there for a long time, cut off in the dungeon with a stone cast over them. Joseph, stolen away and imprisoned though he had done nothing, is a picture of his people in captivity.

precepts.text: They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me; waters flowed over mine head; then I said, I am cut off. That is our forefather Jeremiah in the pit. We all have to go through that; write that precept down.
precepts.point: The prophet which prophesieth of peace, when the word of the prophet shall come to pass, then shall the prophet be known that the Lord hath truly sent him. You will be manifest when the mission is accomplished. We have been warning this country over and over, warning our brothers of what is coming; those who take heed will show that this prophet was among us doing his job. That is what you are beginning to see now. That is why we are here, continuing the mission, continually hardening our faces against the wicked.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

precepts.why:
“The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.” That is what you see our leadership doing today: prophesying against many kingdoms, of war, of evil and of pestilence.

And what happened to the prophets of old who did that? “They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me. Waters flowed over mine head; then I said, I am cut off.” That is our forefather Jeremiah in the dungeon, in the pit, the dungeon where there was no water but mire and he sunk in it, for warning the king. We all have to go through that. Write that precept down.

So we do not stop. We are on the quest, in Ecuador, in Haiti, in Puerto Rico, going to different countries, because this gospel cannot be stopped; the mission must continue. “The prophet which prophesieth of peace, when the word of the prophet shall come to pass, then shall the prophet be known, that the Lord hath truly sent him.” We have been warning this country and our brothers over and over of what is coming. Those who take heed will show that this prophet was among us doing his job, and that is what you are beginning to see now. So we continue the mission, continually hardening our faces against the wicked, even if it leads to the dungeon.

precepts.text: My soul hath them still in remembrance and is humbled in me; this I recall to mind, therefore have I hope. It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not; they are new every morning. The Lord is my portion. We ask forgiveness in the Lord's prayer and he gives it, and we keep playing with sin.
precepts.point: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man; God will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able, but will with the temptation make a way to escape. If you understand the joy of the elect you embrace the temptation, because he has your back. He wants you to make it, though there are those appointed to die. Nobody wanted to pay a landlord who tripled the rent in Brooklyn after counting heads across the street; that trial forced us to pool the real estate, carpentry, plumbing, and electrical talent the Lord had among us, and then he blessed us with the building in New York despite the detractors. We never took our eyes off the prize. Do not let anyone take your crown.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
Paul says the things that happened to our fathers “are written for our admonition”. Jeremiah shows how we hold on to them: “My soul hath them still in remembrance, and is humbled in me.” The them is the afflictions and punishments we are supposed to remember for breaking God's commandments in the past, and we are humbled because of it.

“This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope. It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” Do you hear that? That is the love the Lord has for us, his mercy enduring for ever. He loves you, sisters; he loves you, brothers. His compassions and his mercies fail not.

“They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” His mercies are renewed every day, forgiving us. We say the Lord's prayer, we ask the Lord for mercy and to forgive our transgressions, and he does it. And we are still playing with sin.

“The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.” So now we are in the posture where he has given us a way to escape the evil all around us.

precepts.text: It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed.
precepts.point: Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers. Our help is in the name of the Lord.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
King David says, “If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, now may Israel say”: the Lord was on Israel’s side, “when men rose up against us”, when the nations rose up against us. Think about that. The only reason we are still breathing is the mercy of the Lord.

Lamentations says it plainly: “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” That we, brothers and sisters, are still here is only because of the Lord. With the weapons Esau has and the weapons the nations have, if the Lord put the spirit on them to do what they do and gave them free reign with us, we would all have been wiped out.

Read on: “They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” “The Lord is my portion, saith my soul”. His compassion does not fail, and that is why Psalms 124 can say the nations did not swallow us up.

precepts.text: It is of the Most High's mercies that we are not consumed, His compassions fail not and are new every morning.
precepts.point: We praise the Most High among the nations now by wearing the fringes and beautiful garments, pushing the gospel in the streets to our people, waking up the dead state of our people while Bishop destroys Christianity week after week.
precepts.why:
“For thy mercy is great unto the heavens, and thy truth unto the clouds.” “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” It is of the Most High's mercies that we are not consumed; his compassions fail not and are new every morning.

That is why David says “I myself will awake early” to praise him. His mercy is great unto the heavens and new every morning, so the fixed heart sings and gives praise among the people and among the nations.

precepts.text: All our enemies have opened their mouths against us, and these enemies are the nations.
precepts.point: They compassed me about also with words of hatred and fought against me without a cause. For my love they are my adversaries, but I give myself unto prayer. We have to give ourselves unto prayer and let God fight our battles, for it is not by our might.
precepts.why:
“For the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are opened against me: they have spoken against me with a lying tongue.” Jeremiah says the same in the captivity: “All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.”

The people speaking against us with a lying tongue are the nations. They are the enemies whose mouths are opened against us, compassing us about with words of hatred and fighting against us without a cause.

precepts.text: It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not; they are new every morning, great is Thy faithfulness.
precepts.point: Gracious is the Lord, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful. Our God is merciful, and this is why we are not consumed.

note.label: Psalm 116: I Love the Lord Because He Hath Heard My Voice

precepts.why:
“Gracious is the Lord, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful.” Because he is merciful, we are still here: “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.”

Our God is merciful, and this is why we are not consumed. When the sorrows of death compassed us and the pains of hell got hold on us, we called upon the name of the Lord, and his compassions did not fail; they are new every morning.

precepts.text: The Most High will put all these curses upon our enemies and on them that hate and persecute us.
precepts.point: Jeremiah prayed for the Most High's curse on the enemy because he knew the heathen would have to go through the curses of Deuteronomy 28 when it is all said and done; we are the ones redeemed from the curse, and we will see our enemies go through it for eternity while we reign forever.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

precepts.why:
Jeremiah prays, “Render unto them a recompence, O Lord, according to the work of their hands. Give them sorrow of heart, thy curse unto them.” He prayed for the Most High's curse on the enemy because he knew what was written: “And the Lord thy God will put all these curses upon thine enemies, and on them that hate thee, which persecuted thee.”

The heathen will have to go through the curses of Deuteronomy 28 when it is all said and done. The Most High will put all these curses upon our enemies and on them that hate and persecute us; that is the recompence according to the work of their hands, and Jeremiah asked for it out of the low dungeon.

precepts.text: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, so Israel alone is delivered from the curses of Deuteronomy while the other nations must go through them.
precepts.point: Jeremiah prayed for the Most High's curse on the enemy because he knew the heathen would have to go through the curses of Deuteronomy 28 when it is all said and done; we are the ones redeemed from the curse, and we will see our enemies go through it for eternity while we reign forever.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

precepts.why:
“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree.”

We are the ones redeemed from the curse; Israel alone is delivered from the curses of Deuteronomy, while the other nations must go through them. That is why Jeremiah could pray, “Give them sorrow of heart, thy curse unto them. Persecute and destroy them in anger from under the heavens of the Lord.” The Most High pleaded the causes of his soul and redeemed his life, and we will see our enemies go through the curse for eternity while we reign forever.

precepts.text: It is of the Most High's mercies that we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not, and that is the compassion we are reading about here.
precepts.point: When He is pacified, she shall remember her ways, be ashamed, and never open her mouth anymore because of her shame, and she shall know that He is the Lord.

note.label: Ezekiel 16: The Harlot Redeemed by an Everlasting Covenant

precepts.why:
After everything she has done, the Most High still says, “Nevertheless I will remember my covenant with thee in the days of thy youth, and I will establish unto thee an everlasting covenant.” Why is she not simply wiped out? “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.”

That is the compassion we are reading about here. His compassions fail not, so the harlot is redeemed. He establishes His covenant with her, she shall know that He is the Lord, and He is pacified toward her for all that she has done.

This everlasting covenant, the new covenant of Hebrews 10 and Jeremiah 31, is made only with His people. The notion that our oppressors, who glorified our fall, get the same reward is absolute foolishness and makes no biblical sense. The mercy is toward the one He has a covenant with from the days of her youth.

To give us an example of what it means to mourn. “All our enemies have opened their mouths against us. Fear and a snare is come upon us, desolation and destruction.” Watch this. “Mine eye runneth down with rivers of water” That's crying. “for the destruction of the daughter of my people. Mine eye trickleth down, and ceaseth not,” So the tears kept coming down Jeremiah's face; it said and ceaseth not. “without any intermission,” He could not stop crying when he saw the destruction of his black people.

“Till the Lord look down, and behold from heaven.” That's what he had to wait for. He had to wait for the Lord. That's what we got to do. We can't jump up and do something. When we see images like this, it hurts inside; it makes some of us cry. But we know we can't do nothing. We have to wait for the Lord to make his return.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why:
“Wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?” That is a question Jeremiah is asking: wherefore doth a living man complain? What are you complaining for? A man for the punishment of his sins: you did wrong and you are complaining.

“Let us search and try our ways,” You see what he says here: this is the same thing Christ is saying when he says remember how you have heard and received. Let us search and try our ways. “and turn again to the Lord.” And turn again. Why? Because you are at a point of backsliding. You see your life unfolding before your eyes; things are just going wrong. Let us search and try our ways: that means examine yourself. That is what Christ was saying to the pastor of Sardis. Examine yourselves.

points: It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. Surely without him we would have been destroyed by this white man. We would have been gone off the face of the earth, because that is his goal, that is his aim, that is his perpetual hatred. When you go back to Genesis 27 and read it, he was angry and said to himself, when my father dies, surely I am going to kill this dude, I am going to get my revenge on him. And he has been trying to get it ever since. But surely, of the Lord's mercies, we are not consumed. With all the power that this man has on his side from the spiritual demon Satan, with all the weapons he has, he rules the world, and black and Latino people have nothing to protect ourselves behind enemy lines. How do you think we survived to this day? It is the Lord on our side. So do not ever think that white man smiling in your face actually loves you, black woman. It is the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed as a people.

It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. That is the only reason we are all still here. It is not due to Martin Luther King Jr., it is not due to Malcolm X, or even H. Rap Brown. It is the Lord's compassion.
They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness. The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.
The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.

Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord. Now, right there, that part right there, let us search and try our ways. This is a lot of times what we as a people do not want to do: examine ourselves. What is wrong with me? What is wrong with you? Who raised you? Why do you act that way? Why do you do the things that you do?
Let us lift up our heart with our hands unto God in the heavens.
We have transgressed and have rebelled: thou hast not pardoned. See that? That is why we are in this state, the condition we are in now.
Thou hast covered with anger, and persecuted us: thou hast slain, thou hast not pitied.

Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through. And that part right there, I have seen videos with pastors and Christians, or ex-pastors, ex-Christians, that said, why did God not help us during the time of slavery? Read it again. We have transgressed and have rebelled, thou hast not pardoned. Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through. That is why the Lord let all that stuff happen to us. But through all that he said, I am not going to allow them to destroy you all totally.

People say, I am praying. That pastor said his niece had brain cancer. He prayed and prayed, fasted and fasted, and God still allowed her to die, and he lost his faith as a result. Sometimes the Lord is not hearing our prayers. Why? Because of the way we are, the things we do. So what happens, happens. Get mad if you want. King David understood that when he committed adultery with Bathsheba and they had the baby, God told David, your baby, I am going to kill that child. What did David do? He prayed. He fasted. He cried. God still took the child. What did David do? Wiped his eyes, washed up, went and had some supper. They said, how come now that the baby died you want to eat? He said, there is nothing I can do now. God made his call. He made his decision. That is it. That is how we all have to be like King David was. Do not be like these fake Christians and pastors: oh, God killed my mama, so now I hate God, I hate what the Bible says. You know the souls of our people do not die.

Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people. Looked up in class: offscouring is a rare noun that means physical dirt or refuse cleaned off an object, or a person rejected by society as an outcast. Literal waste, dirt, grime or scum scrubbed off a dirty surface. Social outcast, a person treated as scum, trash, or a pariah by society. Biblical use found in older translations like the King James Bible, such as 1 Corinthians 4:13 and Lamentations 3:45, to describe how lowly or despised the apostles and the people of Jerusalem felt.
All our enemies have opened their mouths against us. All our enemies in the other nations.
Fear and a snare is come upon us, desolation and destruction.
Mine eye runneth down with rivers of water for the destruction of the daughter of my people. Meaning we are crying.

Mine eye trickleth down, and ceaseth not, without any intermission. Because we are crying, and our eyes do not cease to cry. There is no intermission. There is no stopping. Every day is something new.
Till the Lord look down, and behold from heaven. That is what we have to wait for. We must be patient with that.
Mine eye affecteth mine heart because of all the daughters of my city. Our crying affects the way we feel.
Mine enemies chased me sore, like a bird, without cause.

They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me. You know a dungeon is prison. They have cut off my life in the dungeon. That is prison, not jail. It is prison. And cast a stone upon me, meaning you are never getting out. You are in there for life. You have many black political prisoners never getting out. Not that they committed a crime. They have been fraudulently held in there for no reason.
Waters flowed over mine head; then I said, I am cut off.
I called upon thy name, O Lord, out of the low dungeon. That is all we can do. Out of prison, call upon the name of the Lord.
Thou hast heard my voice: hide not thine ear at my breathing, at my cry. Then the Lord said, I heard his voice.
Thou drewest near in the day that I called upon thee: thou saidst, Fear not.
O Lord, thou hast pleaded the causes of my soul; thou hast redeemed my life. Only God can plead our cause.
O Lord, thou hast seen my wrong: judge thou my cause. Thou hast seen my wrong, my sin. Judge thou my cause.

Behold their sitting down, and their rising up; I am their musick. I want you all to examine that verse. You know what they are saying? From the time they sit down, go to sleep, and wake up, they are talking about black people. That is why when you move around in neighbourhoods, what are you doing? Why are you here? What does your t-shirt say? What are your kids doing? We call them Karens and male Karens. But that is what the verse is talking about.
Render unto them a recompence, O Lord, according to the work of their hands. This is what all of us should be praying. A recompence, meaning judgment.
Give them sorrow of heart, thy curse unto them. Give the nations, give the white man, sorrow of heart.

Persecute and destroy them in anger from under the heavens of the Lord. That is Bible right there. Churches are not going to read that. But that is how all of us should feel. All of us should have that faith in that thing right there.

My eye runneth down with rivers of water for the destruction of the daughter of my people. Hands up, don't shoot. Unarmed, busted into their houses, no search warrant. You got ICE out and about collecting our people, some of them actually citizens, being taken to foreign states, being dropped off. Cell phones being taken. All this is going on, and it's natural for us as repenting Israelites caught up in the midst of this to have that sympathy and empathy for our people in the world who being mistreated.

Mine eye trickleth down, and ceaseth not, without any intermission: non-stop crying for our people. Till the Lord look down, and behold from heaven: he understood that. Listen, this thing is of the Lord; I got to wait on the Lord. He says, I'm going to cry until the Lord look down. We can't take it upon ourselves to take up matters into our own hands, or join ourselves and attach ourselves to certain causes prematurely. We got to be very, very mindful.
It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning. Those compassions are the grace we have to renew ourselves every day.

points: His mercies are new every morning. Renew your spirit with prayer when you wake up, morning, noon and evening; shalom to your wife and children, then prayer, not the sports highlights.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

points: The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him. Not your wife, not your children: the Lord is your portion and the only thing to depend on day in and day out.

A hundred dollars no longer buys a week of groceries and it will only get worse. Do not pray for it to get better; pray for it to get worse, because that is when salvation comes. Hope in the Lord shows itself by preparing now, mentally with Messiah, physically with food, shelter and emergency money, and spiritually in the word daily. Ask the Lord to increase your faith and help your unbelief.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: The Most High has hedged him about with gall and travail, set him in dark places like the dead of old, made his chain heavy, and shut out his prayer.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: He has enclosed his ways with hewn stone and made his paths crooked.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: The Most High was to him as a bear lying in wait and a lion in secret places, turning aside his ways, pulling him in pieces, and making him desolate.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: He bent His bow and set him as a mark for the arrow, filled him with bitterness, made him drunken with wormwood, and broke his teeth with gravel stones.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: He covered him with ashes and removed his soul far from peace, so that he forgot prosperity and said his strength and hope had perished from the Most High.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: Remembering his affliction and misery, the wormwood and the gall, his soul is humbled in him.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: This he recalls to mind, therefore he has hope: it is of the Most High's mercies that we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not and are new every morning; great is His faithfulness.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: The Most High is his portion, saith his soul, therefore he will hope in Him.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: The Most High is good to them that wait for Him and to the soul that seeks Him, and it is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Most High.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: It is good for a man to bear the yoke in his youth, to sit alone and keep silence, and to put his mouth in the dust if so be there may be hope.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: He gives his cheek to him that smites him and is filled full with reproach; this points to Christ, who gave His cheek to the smiters, as recorded in the book of Matthew.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: The Most High will not cast off forever; though He causes grief, yet will He have compassion according to the multitude of His mercies, for He does not afflict willingly nor grieve the children of men.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: To crush underfoot the prisoners of the earth, to turn aside the right of a man before the face of the Most High, and to subvert a man in his cause, the Most High approves not.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: Who is he that says and it comes to pass when the Most High commands it not? No prophet can say a thing to come to pass unless the Most High puts His spirit on him; that is how powerful He is, and it is why Israel were the greatest nation on earth, for out of His mouth proceeds both evil and good.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: Why does a living man complain for the punishment of his sins? Let us search and try our ways and turn again to the Most High, instead of only complaining about our conditions while we still dwell in sin.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: We have transgressed and rebelled, and He has not pardoned.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: The Most High covered Himself with anger and persecuted them, covered Himself with a cloud that their prayer should not pass through, and made them as the offscouring in the midst of the people.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: All their enemies opened their mouths against them, and fear and a snare, desolation and destruction came upon them, so that his eye runs down with rivers of water for the destruction of his people.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: The enemies chased him like a bird, cut off his life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon him, and the waters flowed over his head until he said he was cut off.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: He called on the Most High's name out of the low dungeon, and He heard his voice and drew near in the day he called, saying, Fear not; the Most High pleaded the causes of his soul and redeemed his life.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

points: He asks the Most High to judge his cause, having seen all the enemies' vengeance and imaginations against him, and to render them a recompense according to the work of their hands, giving them sorrow of heart and His curse.
